name: Sim0 Prop 65 Warnings for WooCommerce
author: joesimo

sections.description:
California’s Proposition 65 (Prop 65) asks businesses to give a California warning about exposure to listed chemicals. For online sales, that warning has to reach the shopper before the purchase, for example on the product page.

Sim0 Prop 65 Warnings for WooCommerce adds a Prop 65 tab to the product editor. You pick what the warning is for and type the chemical names, and the plugin writes the California warning text from the safe-harbor wording in 27 CCR 25603 (and 27 CCR 25607.2 for food). The warning then shows on the product page with the signal word, the warning triangle and a link to www.P65Warnings.ca.gov.

Quick start

  1. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Products > Prop 65 and choose your signal word, default warning form and where the warning shows.
  2. Edit a product and open the Prop 65 tab in the Product data box.
  3. Set Prop 65 warning to Show a warning.
  4. Choose cancer, reproductive harm, or both, and enter at least one chemical name, for example lead.
  5. Update the product. The Saved warning preview under the fields shows the exact text shoppers will see.

Per product

  • Turn the warning on or off for each product
  • Consumer product or food (food and dietary supplements get the food wording, the www.P65Warnings.ca.gov/food link and no symbol)
  • Cancer, reproductive harm, or both (different chemicals or one chemical listed for both)
  • Short form, full-length form, or the old short form for products made and labeled before January 1, 2028
  • Optional custom warning text, for wording your supplier or advisor gave you
  • For a variable product, one warning covers all of its variations

Store settings

  • Signal word: WARNING:, CA WARNING: or CALIFORNIA WARNING:
  • Default warning form and short form wording (“Cancer risk from exposure to…” or “Can expose you to…”)
  • Show the warning below the price or below the add to cart button
  • Yellow or black and white warning triangle
  • Opt-in clean uninstall

Other details

  • Works with classic themes and with block themes that use the WooCommerce single product template
  • Declares compatibility with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and the Cart and Checkout blocks
  • No tracking, no ads, no external requests. Translation ready (the warning wording itself stays in English, as written in the regulation)
  • Developer filters: sim0p65_product_warning_data, sim0p65_warning and sim0p65_settings

Important

This plugin helps you display Prop 65 warnings. It is not legal advice. It does not decide whether a product needs a warning, which chemicals to name, or whether the warning also has to be on the product label or packaging. Check your obligations with a qualified advisor.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Sim0 Prop 65 Warnings for WooCommerce”, then install and activate it.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Products > Prop 65 and check the store settings.
  4. Edit a product, open the Prop 65 tab in the Product data box, choose Show a warning, fill in the fields and update the product.
sections.faq:
I activated the plugin but my shoppers see nothing. What do I do?

Nothing shows until a Prop 65 warning is set up on a product. After activation, a short notice on the Plugins screen links to your newest product: open the Prop 65 tab in the Product data box, choose Show a warning and enter the chemical name, then update the product. The notice goes away once that is done, or for good when you dismiss it. The plugin shows no notices on other admin screens. The settings page also says whether anything is showing yet.

What is a California warning or Prop 65 warning?

A California warning, also called a Proposition 65 or Prop 65 warning, is the notice California law asks businesses to give before exposing someone to listed chemicals. This plugin helps you display that warning label on the product page. It does not decide whether a product needs a warning or which chemicals to name.

Where are the settings?

WooCommerce > Settings > Products > Prop 65.

Where does the warning appear for shoppers?

On the single product page, below the price or below the add to cart button, depending on the Product page setting. This works in classic themes such as Storefront and in block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five.

Why don’t I see a warning on a product?

Check that the product’s Prop 65 warning is set to Show a warning and that the chemical names the chosen form needs are filled in. The short form and the full-length form need at least one chemical name. When both cancer and reproductive harm apply with different chemicals, both chemical fields need a name. The Saved warning preview in the Prop 65 tab tells you when something is missing.

Can food products use the short form?

Yes. 27 CCR 25607.2(b) has a food short form with the same wording as the consumer short form and the www.P65Warnings.ca.gov/food link, without the symbol. There is no old short form for food, so a food product set to Old short form shows the full-length food warning.

Can I change the wording?

Use the Custom warning text field on a product, or the sim0p65_warning filter.

Can I set a different warning for each variation?

Not in this plugin. The warning set on a variable product covers all of its variations.

Does the plugin send any data anywhere?

No. It makes no external requests and does not track anything. All data stays in your WordPress database.

Is data removed when I delete the plugin?

Only if you tick “Remove data on uninstall” in the settings before deleting the plugin. This protects your warnings if you delete and reinstall.

1.0.3

1.0.2
